Definition: concretely, crushed; also afraid; abstractly, terror
BiblicalUsage: This word is fear and terror, and also the shattering that fear brings. God puts the fear and dread of man on every beast after the flood, Hannah sings that the bows of the mighty are broken, Isaiah warns that Ephraim will be broken, and Leviathan is described as made without fear.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fear belongs in its right place: beasts fear man, the mighty are broken, and only Leviathan fears nothing. The fear of the LORD is the one fear that steadies a man instead of shattering him.
RelatedEvents: Noah and the Flood; Calling of Samuel; The Sign to Ahaz
